newsitem.title: GERMANY: UPS German works council attacks union protests.
newsitem.headline: UPS German works council attacks union protests.

text.p: The United Parcel Service of America German works council said it did not back transport union protests at UPS sites in Germany.
Works council chairman Thomas Wilms accused striking American Teamsters, the International Transport Federation and the German transport OeTV of "self-promotion" at protests last week.
The OeTV held solidarity actions at several UPS locations last week and warned on August 14 it was considering stepping up sympathy actions for the Teamsters strike, now in its second week.
But in a four-page open letter supplied to Reuters, Wilms claimed the democratically-elected German works council had not been consulted before the protest actions but deliberately ignored.
The German works council is responsible for representing the 14,000 UPS employees in Germany.

"The public actions in Germany do not have the support of a majority of works councils and the workers. (They) serve primarily a trade union's self-prmotion but not necessarily the interests of the employees," he said.
Union criticism of part-time work and sub-contracting at UPS Germany was unjustified and exaggerated since the firm paid above-average wages to full- and part-time staff, Wilms said.
The works council had reluctantly accepted some limited sub-contracting but only to firms with full-time drivers, he added.
